usage:
ocho-tui: a full-screen terminal interface for ocho. Pick with the arrow keys instead of remembering flags.

Usage  ocho-tui [flags]

With no flags it opens Home: saved contexts, adding one, connecting with a URL, opening a snapshot, rules and codes.
With --context, --url, --from (or OCHO_URL, OCHO_CONTEXT) it opens doctor on that broker right away.
It takes the same flags as ocho doctor: --context, --url, --user, --ca, --insecure, --prometheus-url, --no-prometheus, --max-rps, --concurrency, --vhost, --flow, --target-version, --fail-on, --file, --no-file, --from, --experimental, --lang.

Keys: arrows to move, Enter to open, Esc to go back, ? for help on every screen, L to switch language, q to quit.
For scripts and CI use ocho (JSON, exit codes).

Read-only: this tool never writes to the broker.
refused_flag: --{flag} is for scripts; use ocho for it
needs_tty: ocho-tui needs an interactive terminal; in scripts and CI use ocho
help.title: Help
help.tip1: Every result shows the ocho command that gives the same output, dimmed at the top. Copy it into scripts and CI.
help.tip2: Ocho only reads. Nothing here writes to the broker; only Import writes a file (ocho.yaml), and only after you confirm.
help.tip3: Passwords you type stay in memory until you quit. To skip typing, set a password command on the context.
password.title: Password needed
password.note: Kept in memory until you quit; never written to disk. To skip this, add a password command to the context.
password.retry.CX3: The broker rejected that password. Try again.
password.retry.CX7: The password command failed. Type the password instead.
home.title: Brokers
home.welcome: No saved broker yet. Pick "Add a context" to save one, or "Connect with a URL" to try one now.
home.menu_title: {name}: what do you want to do?
home.action.explain: Explain a queue, exchange or flow…
home.action_hint.doctor: find where messages can be lost
home.action_hint.explain: effective settings and the rules on it
home.action_hint.import: declare flows and how much loss each can take
home.action_hint.use: used when no broker is named
home.about.add: Save a broker as a context: URL, user, and optionally a command that prints the password (for example op read …). Ocho checks the connection before saving and never stores the password itself.
home.about.connect: Run doctor on a broker without saving it. You will be asked for the password.
home.about.snapshot: Read a snapshot saved earlier (ocho doctor --save, or s in doctor). Works offline; useful to share a report or attach to an issue.
home.about.rules: Browse every rule, blind spot and diagnostic code with its explanation. No broker needed.
home.about.cli: The broker named by the flags or environment variables ocho-tui started with.
home.about.url: A broker reached by URL, not saved as a context.
context.confirm_remove: Remove context {name}? Its password command goes with it; the broker is not touched.
add.title: Add a context
add.intro: A context is a saved broker. Ocho connects once to check it, then saves it in the context file with mode 0600. Only the password command is saved, never the password.
add.name: Name
add.name_hint: Lowercase letters, digits, . _ -; for example prod or staging.
add.url_hint: Management API URL, http or https, without a password in it.
add.user_hint: A user with the monitoring tag is enough; Ocho only reads.
add.password_command_hint: Optional. A command whose first line of output is the password. Leave empty to be asked each time.
add.prometheus_hint: Optional URL of /metrics; leave empty to find it automatically.
add.ca_hint: Optional PEM file for a private certificate authority.
add.insecure_hint: Only for testing; every run warns about it (CX5).
add.verify_hint: Recommended: nothing is saved if the broker cannot be reached.
add.bad_name: Use lowercase letters, digits, . _ -, starting with a letter or digit.
connect.title: Connect with a URL
connect.intro: Run doctor on a broker without saving it. You will be asked for the password.
snapshot.title: Open a snapshot
snapshot.intro: A snapshot is a broker reading saved to a file (.json or .json.gz). Doctor reads it without connecting to anything.
options.title: Doctor options
options.intro: Leave a field empty to keep the default.
options.vhost_hint: Comma separated, for example payments, orders. Only these are read.
options.fail_on_hint: Lowest severity that counts as a failure in the exit code (S1 is the most severe).
options.target_version_hint: Planning an upgrade? Adds the rules for that version, for example 4.2.
options.flow_hint: Check only one flow from ocho.yaml.
options.file_hint: Path to the flow declarations; empty uses ./ocho.yaml if it exists.
options.experimental_hint: Include rules that are still being tuned; they never change the exit code.
doctor.title: Doctor
doctor.read_only: Read-only: nothing is written to the broker. Esc stops safely.
doctor.passed_intro: These rules ran and found nothing wrong (count of objects per rule):
doctor.blind_intro: Ways to lose messages that no broker reading can show: they live in client code or in decisions. Enter on a code in Rules and codes explains each.
doctor.no_object: This item is not about a single queue or exchange.
doctor.object_needs_broker: Explaining an object reads the broker; not available for a snapshot.
save.title: Save a snapshot
save.intro: Saves this broker reading to a file so it can be read later without the broker: ocho doctor --from <file>. Ends in .gz to compress.
save.redact_hint: Replaces host and connection names with hashes; good before sharing.
export.title: Export the report as JSON
export.intro: Writes the same ocho.report/1 document as ocho doctor --json, for scripts and dashboards.
explain.title: Explain
explain_object.title: Explain an object
explain_object.intro: Shows each effective setting of a queue or exchange, where it comes from (argument, policy, default), and the rules on it. Reads only that object: fast even on big brokers.
explain_object.name: Name
import.title: Import
import.intro: Reads the topology (exchanges, queues, bindings) and writes ocho.yaml: which flows exist and how much message loss each can take. You answer one question per flow; Enter keeps the default. Nothing is written until you confirm at the end.
import.out_hint: An existing file is updated; your edits to it are kept.
import.source_hint: A definitions export (rabbitmqadmin export) works without broker access.
import.tolerance.undeclared.about: Not decided yet. Doctor checks only the structure of this flow. You can change it in ocho.yaml any time.
import.tolerance.strict.about: No message may be lost in this flow: payments, orders. Any way to lose one becomes an S1 finding.
import.tolerance.loose.about: Losing a message here is acceptable: metrics, caches, notifications that are resent.
import.tolerance.exchange: Same answer for the rest of this exchange…
import.tolerance.exchange.about: Answers this flow and every remaining flow on the same exchange at once.
import.apply_rest: Tolerance for the rest of this exchange:
import.family_choice.skip.about: Keep these queues as separate flows.
import.family_choice.accept.about: Write one family with a name template instead of one flow per queue; doctor checks every member the same way, including queues created later.
import.family_choice.rename.about: Like accept, with your own name for the varying part of the queue name (a-z, 0-9, _).
import.member_choice.skip.about: Leave the member list as it is.
import.member_choice.add.about: Doctor then checks this queue like the other members.
import.confirm_stop: Stop the import? Nothing will be written.
import.confirm_defaults: Use the default answer for every remaining question? Flows stay undeclared, families are skipped.
import.review_summary: {flows, plural, one {# flow} other {# flows}}: {strict} strict, {loose} loose, {undeclared} undeclared · {families, plural, one {# family} other {# families}}
import.review_confirm: Enter writes {file}; Esc stops without writing.
import.done_next: Next: run doctor (d) to check the broker against these declarations.
